pages.intro_p1: The names sound alike, but BetterWorld and Better Giving are separate organizations that do different jobs. If your year builds up to a gala, BetterWorld is a strong fit. You can run online, mobile and live auctions, giveaways and ticketed events on its Free Forever plan, and donors can choose to add a contribution to keep it running. Extras like automatic payouts sit on paid plans, which start at $1,550 a year plus 1.25%.
pages.intro_p2: Better Giving has no auction or raffle tools, so it plays a different part. It gives you one donation form on your own website for card, bank, PayPal, stock, DAF, IRA and crypto gifts, and it stays free while the optional donor donation to Better Giving is on. Money reaches your bank within 5 working days, and anything you leave in savings earns a little over 3%. You could use both, BetterWorld for the gala and Better Giving for the rest of the year.

sections.h2: Running a gala or auction on BetterWorld
sections.text: BetterWorld's Free Forever plan covers online, mobile and live auctions, giveaways and event tickets, and Better Giving has no auction tools. If your year centers on a gala, BetterWorld is a good home for the event itself. Your everyday, recurring, stock and crypto gifts can still come through a Better Giving donation form, with reserves in savings that earn a little over 3%.

sections.h2: When BetterWorld is the better choice
sections.text: Pick BetterWorld when auctions, raffles, giveaways or ticketed events drive most of your fundraising. BetterWorld designed its tools for those nights, and the Free Forever plan costs nothing in platform fees. Using both is a reasonable setup, BetterWorld for event nights and Better Giving for gifts the rest of the year.

faq.q: Are Better Giving and BetterWorld the same company?
faq.a: No. They are separate organizations with similar names. BetterWorld describes itself as a social impact venture and focuses on auctions, giveaways and events. Better Giving is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit, EIN 87-3758939, focused on donation forms, savings and fiscal sponsorship.

faq.q: Is BetterWorld free?
faq.a: BetterWorld has a Free Forever plan with a 0% platform fee. It asks donors for an optional contribution, and card processing through Stripe costs 2.9% + $0.30. Better Giving also charges no platform fee while the optional donor donation stays on, and 1.5% if you turn it off.

faq.q: Which platform is better for auctions?
faq.a: BetterWorld. Auctions and giveaways are core BetterWorld products, and Better Giving offers neither.

faq.q: Can I use both?
faq.a: Yes. A nonprofit could run its auction on BetterWorld and use the Better Giving donation form on its website for everyday, recurring, stock and crypto gifts.

faq.q: Does BetterWorld offer savings or an endowment?
faq.a: We found no savings or endowment product on BetterWorld's public pages. Better Giving lets you send a share of each gift to savings that earn a little over 3% or to the Sustainability Fund.

It tracks insights, segments and journeys, and the fundraising add-on brings auctions and peer-to-peer pages, with payouts arriving daily. You do pay for all that. The add-on starts at $40 a month on top of the CRM at $125, both billed annually, and cards on its fundraising donation forms cost 3.95% + $0.30. We don't have a full CRM, so you'd export donor records by CSV or API into whichever one you use. At entry prices, Bloomerang's two subscriptions add up to $1,980 a year before card fees, which is worth knowing before you sign.
